subtype: Approach: comparing with a peer's path without context [Pitfall]
passage:
Indu: You copied a colleague's promotion path?

Gurleen: Every step. Yogesh got promoted in two years: a training course, one big presentation, then a move to the platform team. So I took the same course, gave the same kind of presentation, and asked for the same move. Two years went by. Nothing. I was angry, then confused, and only then did I look at what was different. His team had doubled in size and three senior posts had opened. Mine hasn't grown in years, so there was no senior post to move into. He followed a path that fitted his team. I followed his path in a team where it led nowhere.

qa.q: How long did it take Yogesh to be promoted?
qa.a: Yogesh got promoted in two years.

qa.q: What was Gurleen feeling when nothing happened after two years?
qa.a: Gurleen was angry and then confused, until seeing what was different.

qa.q: What else could Gurleen do to plan a promotion, and why?
qa.a: Gurleen could ask the manager what senior posts might open in this team and build a plan from that, because the path has to fit where the team is heading.

qa.q: How might Yogesh have seen his own promotion?
qa.a: Yogesh probably saw it as the result of his own effort and did not think about how much the growing team helped.

grounding: Illustrates copying a colleague's promotion steps without noticing that the colleague's team was growing and the narrator's was not, so the same path gives no equal opportunity.
